llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Inconel 718合金的晶界网络演化，与生物医学植入物设计、应力屏蔽或骨整合无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures for stress shielding, LPBF fabrication with biomedical mechanical testing, fatigue behavior, or osseointegration; it focuses on grain boundary evolution in a nickel superalloy for aerospace applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究选区激光熔融Inconel 718合金晶界网络的演化。
summary_zh.method: 通过电子背散射衍射（EBSD）表征不同热处理状态的晶界特征。
summary_zh.result: 发现了热处理对晶界类型和分布的影响规律。
summary_zh.validation: 实验表征，无生物医学相关验证。

summary_en.motivation: To understand how the grain boundary network evolves in selective laser melted Inconel 718 during post-processing heat treatments.
summary_en.method: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) was used to characterize grain boundary character distribution in as-built and heat-treated samples.
summary_en.result: Heat treatments significantly altered the fraction of low-angle and special boundaries, affecting material properties.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization via EBSD, no mechanical or biomedical testing.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究热处理对SLM成形CoCrMo合金性能的影响，优化植入物力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 通过选区激光熔化制备CoCrMo试样，并进行不同热处理工艺。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of heat treatment on the mechanical and microstructural properties of CoCrMo alloy fabricated by selective laser melting for biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: CoCrMo specimens were manufactured by selective laser melting and subjected to various heat treatment cycles (solution treatment and aging).
summary_en.result: Heat treatment significantly altered the microstructure (grain size, phase distribution) and improved mechanical properties such as hardness and tensile strength.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through standard mechanical testing including tensile tests, hardness measurements, and microstructural characterization.

papers.title: Perfusion-decellularization of human ear grafts enables ECM-based scaffolds for auricular vascularized composite tissue engineering
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human ear reconstruction is recognized as the emblematic enterprise in tissue engineering. Up to now, it has failed to reach human applications requiring appropriate tissue complexity along with an accessible vascular tree. We hereby propose a new method to process human auricles in order to provide a poorly immunogenic, complex and vascularized ear graft scaffold. METHODS: 12 human ears with their vascular pedicles were procured. Perfusion-decellularization was applied using a SDS/polar solvent protocol. Cell and antigen removal was examined by histology and DNA was quantified. Preservation of the extracellular matrix (ECM) was assessed by conventional and 3D-histology, proteins and cytokines quantifications. Biocompatibility was assessed by implantation in rats for up to 60 days. Adipose-derived stem cells seeding was conducted on scaffold samples and with human aortic endothelial cells whole graft seeding in a perfusion-bioreactor. RESULTS: Histology confirmed cell and antigen clearance. DNA reduction was 97.3%. ECM structure and composition were preserved. Implanted scaffolds were tolerated in vivo, with acceptable inflammation, remodeling, and anti-donor antibody formation. Seeding experiments demonstrated cell engraftment and viability. CONCLUSIONS: Vascularized and complex auricular scaffolds can be obtained from human source to provide a platform for further functional auricular tissue engineered constructs, hence providing an ideal road to the vascularized composite tissue engineering approach. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: The ear is emblematic in the biofabrication of tissues and organs. Current regenerative medicine strategies, with matrix from donor tissues or 3D-printed, didn't reach any application for reconstruction, because critically missing a vascular tree for perfusion and transplantation. We previously described the production of vascularized and cell-compatible scaffolds, from porcine ear grafts. In this study, we ---- applied findings directly to human auricles harvested from postmortem donors, providing a perfusable matrix that retains the ear's original complexity and hosts new viable cells after seeding. This approach unlocks the ability to achieve an auricular tissue engineering approach, associated with possible clinical translation.

summary_zh.motivation: 人耳重建需要血管化复杂支架，当前方法缺乏血管网络。
summary_zh.method: 采用灌注脱细胞技术处理人耳，保留ECM结构并去除细胞和抗原。
summary_zh.result: 成功获得血管化人耳ECM支架，DNA去除97.3%，体内植入耐受良好。
summary_zh.validation: 通过组织学、DNA定量、大鼠植入和细胞接种验证。

summary_en.motivation: Human ear reconstruction requires vascularized complex scaffolds, which current methods fail to provide.
summary_en.method: Human auricles were perfusion-decellularized using SDS/polar solvent protocol to remove cells while preserving ECM.
summary_en.result: Vascularized auricular ECM scaffolds were obtained with 97.3% DNA removal and showed biocompatibility in rat implantation.
summary_en.validation: Validation included histology, DNA quantification, in vivo rat implantation, and cell seeding in perfusion bioreactor.

papers.title: Total hip arthroplasty following arthrodesis: a single-center experience of 17 patients
papers.abstract: Murat &amp;Ccedil;albÄ±yÄ±k Department of Orthopedics and Traumatology, Hitit University, Faculty of Medicine, Corum, Turkey Purpose: We aimed to present our experience with total hip arthroplasty in patients with previous hip arthrodesis. Patients and methods: This was a retrospective study, in which clinical and radiological outcomes of total hip arthroplasty performed in 17 patients (mean age 54.2&amp;plusmn;8.5 years; age range 33&amp;ndash;68 years; female to male ratio 10/7) with previous arthrodesis in our clinic between 2001 and 2014 were reviewed. Patients were followed up for 6.7&amp;plusmn;2.8 years (range 3&amp;ndash;12 years) after the operation and evaluated for ipsilateral knee pain, range of motion, walking capacity, and leg-length discrepancy. The clinical outcome was assessed by the Harris Hip Score. Results: The outcome of arthroplasty was good or excellent in 14 of 17 patients (82.3%), fair in two patients (11.8%), and failure in one patient (5.9%). The Harris Hip Score increased to 79.8&amp;plusmn;9.8 postoperatively from a preoperative score of 40.9&amp;plusmn;10.1 (p&amp;lt;0.01). Pain-free hip was obtained in 15 patients (88.2%), and range of motion was 88&amp;deg;. Fourteen patients (82.4%) reported a significant decrease in back pain, and 11 patients (64.7%) in ipsilateral knee pain. Ten patients (58.8%) were able to walk normally, five patients (29.4%) walked with slight Trendelenburg gait without support, and two patients (11.8%) with severe Trendelenburg gait using arm rests. The mean leg-length discrepancy was 1.1 cm (range 0&amp;ndash;3 cm). The complications were peroneal nerve palsy (n=3), superficial wound infection (n=3), hip dislocation (n=2), and heterotopic ossification (n=3). Conclusion: If it is well planned, conversion of hip arthrodesis to total hip arthroplasty is a successful and safe procedure, which increases patients&amp;rsquo; functionality. Keywords: hip arthrodesis, total hip arthroplasty, retrospective, range of motion

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate clinical outcomes of converting hip arthrodesis to total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective review of 17 patients with pre-existing hip arthrodesis who underwent THA.
summary_en.result: Good or excellent outcomes in 82.3% of patients, with significant improvement in Harris Hip Score.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up over an average of 6.7 years, without computational or experimental biomechanical validation.
